categories.words: Up to ₹2 lakh. SME lots are large, so one lot may be all there is.
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 7 applicants gets one lot (an estimate, from 7.5x bids).
categories.note: Applying for more lots doesn't raise your chance: when retail is oversubscribed, each winner gets one lot.

categories.words: More than ₹2 lakh, up to ₹10 lakh.
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 6 applicants gets the smallest application (an estimate, from 5.9x bids).

categories.label: Big HNI (bHNI)
categories.odds_words: About 1 in 4 applicants gets the smallest application (an estimate, from 3.6x bids).

exits.title: Your listing-day rule
steps: Before Fri 6 Nov: decide your rule now, while you're calm, and write it in your journal.
On Fri 6 Nov, the shares start trading at 10 AM. Don't buy more on the first day's excitement.
If it opens above ₹158: you applied for a listing gain, so sell on listing day. Waiting for more turns a plan into a hope.
If it opens below ₹158: sell if it is more than 10% below your price, rather than holding on to wait for it to come back.

exits.title: Your holding plan
steps: You'd be holding for the business, not the first day's price. Look again on the dates below, and sell if a reason you bought stops being true.

reviews.why: The first results after listing: check sales and profit are still growing.
Half a year on: compare the business with what the RHP promised.
One year on: did it beat simply buying the Nifty 50?

breakers: Sales stop growing, or fall, in two results in a row.
The share price runs so far that its P/E is well above its peers'.
Promoters sell a big part of their stake, or pledge their shares, after the lock-in.
The business stops doing what the IPO money was raised for.
The auditor resigns, or adds remarks to the accounts.

disclaimer: A learning aid worked out by fixed rules, not advice. Only apply with money you won't need soon, and decide for yourself.
